newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico main crude ports open - port authorities.
newsitem.headline: Mexico main crude ports open - port authorities.

text.p: Mexico's three main crude ports were reported open Monday morning after two were shut over the weekend because of bad weather, port authorities said Monday.

Officials at the nation's largest crude port, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, said the terminal was not shut over the weekend. This contradicted a Communication and Transport Ministry report on Sunday that said the port had shut.

Pajaritos in Veracruz state reopened at 0800 local/1400 GMT as wind speeds relaxed, a port official told Reuters. At 0645 local/1245 GMT, Dos Bocas in Tabasco state was reopened as weather conditions improved, port authorities said.

Cayo Arcas ships an average 611,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude, Dos Bocas ships 440,000 bpd and Pajaritos ships 399,000 bpd, according to the latest figures from state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
